observations: Torah 111 (LM2) consists of two extremely brief reported episodes. In the first, someone unable to study Torah is told: 'עַל־יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה יְכוֹלִין לָבוֹא לַכֹּל' — through prayer one can arrive at everything, including Torah, avodah, all holiness, all service, and all good in all the worlds. In the second episode the Rebbe says that if a dead person were allowed to return to pray, he would pray beautifully with all his strength. The text contains no bechina language and no conceptual equivalences are declared. The relationship between תְּפִלָּה and תּוֹרָה / עֲבוֹדָה is explicitly eitza (through prayer → one arrives at Torah), not bechina (prayer does not share the essential nature of Torah; it is the vehicle that brings one there). No cluster of three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language exists anywhere in the text. Therefore no new packages are proposed, and the dataset correctly records zero bechina edges for this Torah.
